title: community report batch output (NNN.out.json)
description: The contract between `community-summarizer` and `brain communities merge`. One report per community in the matching `.in.json`, in the Microsoft GraphRAG community-report style: a theme title, a summary of what the cluster is about, and findings that each cite evidence. Merge applies this file in two halves: the ENVELOPE (`batch_id`, `reports` being an array, no unknown top-level field) decides whether the batch is readable at all, and each report under `$defs` is checked on its own — one bad report is rejected and counted, the rest of the batch merges. Three rules merge adds that a schema cannot state: `community_id` must be one of the communities in this batch's `.in.json`, every `evidence_chunk_ids` entry must be one of the `evidence[].chunk_id` values offered for THAT community (a chunk from another community is not evidence about this one), and every community in the input must be answered exactly once.

batch_id.description: Exactly the `batch_id` of the .in.json this answers, e.g. "shard-01/003".

reports.description: One entry per community in the input, in any order. Never a partial file: a community you cannot summarise is a `failed` entry in status.json, not a missing report.

notes.description: Free-text remarks for the report — a community whose members look unrelated, evidence that contradicts itself. Never a place to hide a rule you could not follow.

chunk_id.description: The `chunk_id` of a chunk offered in this community's `evidence[]`, copied exactly (40 hex characters). Merge rejects the report if the id was not offered for this community.

community_id.description: The `community_id` of a community in this batch, copied exactly, e.g. "L0-217".

title.description: At most 10 words naming the THEME, not listing members. "Consumer rebalance protocol migration", not "KIP-848, KAFKA-14048 and three entities".

summary.description: 100-250 words: what this cluster is about, the main tensions and decisions in it, and what is still open. Use only what the input gives you.

findings.description: The specific claims a reader should take away, most important first. Each one cites at least one evidence chunk from THIS community.

rank.description: 0-10: how much this community matters to someone running this organisation — impact, how open it still is, how broadly it reaches.

rank_reason.description: One sentence saying why that rank.

statement.description: One claim, in your own words, that the cited chunks support.

evidence_chunk_ids.description: The chunks that support the statement. At least one; a finding with no evidence is rejected and counted in the report, and that count must be zero.
